_comment: The missions (SPEC.md §12 M27, ROADMAP.md Phase 2): the game is an engine plus a mission. Each entry is printed on the contents page, in this order. `status` is `playable`, `draft` or `coming`; a coming mission is printed but stamped NEXT YEAR'S ANNUAL and cannot be chosen, so it needs only `id`, `title`, `place`, `page` and `blurb`. A draft one (M28) is printed and stamped as a coming one, but `?mission=<id>` plays it, so it can be tried on the live site before it is announced; it needs everything a playable one does. A playable one names its `map` and `roster` files, and a `rules` and `enemies` patch deep-merged over data/rules.json and data/enemies.json before the difficulty's (the same merge difficulty.json uses; a key must already exist, except a new objective kind under `objectives` or a new enemy type under `types`). `win` is one of the fixed win conditions in src/missions.js, never a code branch for one mission. `briefing` opens the orders; `tagline` runs along the foot of the title card; `levels` (M28, optional) is the mission's own part of each difficulty level, keyed by the level's id in data/difficulty.json: a `rules` and `enemies` patch merged after the level's own, and a `summary` printed before the level's; what a level does to this mission's targets lives here, what it does in every mission lives in difficulty.json. `words` are the mission's own phrases the rules' text needs (the cut line's; the diversion's name, card and log line, M31: France's RAF diversion is the airfield's jeep raid; `cleanOrders`, M32c, optional, the operator's: the orders' line about the clean-run bonus, in the mission's words since its condition is the mission's: all night in France, only until the first bang on the airfield); `diversionSound` (M31, optional) is the sound.js cue for the diversion, `diversion` when left out; `dialogue` (M28) replaces any of the men's lines for this mission, keyed by his roster id, over the roster file's; `titleCard` is its painted title card (ART-ASSETS.md §7), France's until the file is there (M31), and `panel` (M31c, optional, any status) is its small painting beside its line on the contents page (ART-ASSETS.md §7); `titleCardLettered` (M31, optional, true when left out) says whether BURN BY DAWN is painted into it, or code must set it; `portraits` (M29b, optional) is a folder of the mission's own portraits, named as in assets/portraits, each tried before the usual one; `enemyChips` (M43, optional) is a folder of the mission's own enemy chips, named as in assets/enemies, each tried before the usual one (the aqueduct's Italians); `counterColour` (M31d, optional, art only) names the theme.js PALETTE colour our men's counters are printed in, army green when left out (the airfield's burnt orange, the operator's: green on the desert sat too close to the garrison's chits); `endSounds` are the sound.js cues for the back page; `ratings` (M32, optional) are the back page's score bands for a mission accomplished, lowest first, each a `from` score and a `label` (src/missions.js ratingOf). `?mission=<id>` in the address picks one, and `default` is the one when none is asked for.

missions.title: The Rail Bridge
missions.blurb: Six men drop by night to blow the bridge that carries the line to the coast, and must be out before dawn.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE BRIDGE · DAWN AT SIXTEEN
missions._rules: M38b: `turnLimit` 16 (the operator's, after a turn at 15; 20 until M38: with the train at 10 the night had five turns of slack; the bot wins as often with dawn at 15, hurrying as it nears, and the Fuel Dump becomes the thing there is rarely time for). M34: France's other patch is its goods train (data/rules.json `train`): on the Rail Bridge in the enemy phase of turn 10 (M37, the operator's: waiting for it at 17 was dull; 14 at first, then 17 from M34b, when waiting for it cost nothing), seen coming on from the west edge three turns before; the bridge down on turn 16, 17 or 18 pays 5 (the operator's: within a turn of it, score only, scenery). Everything else is the files as they are.
missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop behind enemy lines.

hard.summary: Blowing a target calls up reinforcements to guard the way out: two squads for the Rail Bridge, one for the Fuel Dump, none once the Telephone Exchange is down.

words.cleanOrders: Getting in and out with as little enemy attention as possible earns a special bonus!

missions._ratings: M32: the back page's verdict on a mission accomplished, as score bands, lowest first (the first from 0). Set against the bot's winning scores on Normal (tools/balance-bot.mjs with SCORES=1): the bridge alone with most men out lands in the middle two; the top wants the bonus targets or a spotless night. M38b: the top from 40 (was 43), the operator's: with dawn at 16 there is rarely time for the Fuel Dump, and the greedy bot's best quarter of wins score 39 to 42. M34: 28/36/43 (were 24/30/36), for the goods train's 5 and the Fuel Dump's fifth point: the bridge alone wins 24–33, with the train 33–39, with the train and both bonus targets 42–45. Placeholder copy for the operator to reword.

missions.title: The Airfield
missions.blurb: Paratroopers raid aircraft in their pens on an Axis landing ground, ready to blow them sky high.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · EIGHT AIRCRAFT · DAWN AT TWENTY
missions._rules: SPEC.md §13. Lewes bombs are small, so the scouts carry one each as well as the sappers (M29b, the operator's: with none, and two a sapper, the scouts had nothing to do here); still five in the stick with Nunn's. The win pays 10 on top of each aircraft's own 2, since no target here is worth the bridge's 10 on its own. M32: the garrison is Alarmed by the end of every raid here, so the clean run asks only that it was below Alert when the first bang went (and no jeep raid), and the jeep raid is urged only for men in contact, never for the Alarmed garrison. Three new objective kinds; their numbers are Normal's, first guesses for M30's balance.
missions._enemies: The perimeter car (SPEC.md §13): fast, so it reaches a noise first; it can be suppressed but never killed or knifed.

hard.summary: Seven aircraft are wanted: with five bombs, the bowser and the bomb store both have to go.

missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop on an enemy landing ground.
missions._words: M31. The RAF diversion is a jeep raid here (the operator's, M29b): the same rule, in the mission's words, with the map's diversionRun for the jeep's drive past the north wire and its own sound. Placeholder copy for the operator to reword.

words.lineIsDown: the field telephones are already down
words.diversionLog: jeeps shoot up the north wire
words.cleanOrders: Getting in with as little enemy attention as possible earns a special bonus!

missions._dialogue: M31: only the lines that name France or its ground (Fitch's cabbages and dirt, Vance's church, Barrow's trees, bridge and mud).

fitch.onLand: Down soft as you like. Sand in places I'll not mention.
fitch.onHide: Nice and snug in the sand.

vance.onLand: I can see the tails of the aircraft from here. We're about right.

barrow.onLand: Not a tree for a hundred miles. Told you I'd miss them all.
barrow.onWounded: Leave it. Get to the aircraft.
barrow.onHide: Down in the dust, where I belong.

missions._ratings: M32, as France's: five aircraft with most men out lands in the middle two; the top wants more than five, the signals tent and a quiet way in. M33: each band two or three higher, for the bomb store and the salvo (naive wins 35–46 between the quartiles, a careful game going for everything 44–53).

missions.title: The Aqueduct
missions.blurb: A great aqueduct in the mountains that wants every charge you carry, and a boat on the coast that will not wait.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE AQUEDUCT · THE BOAT WILL NOT WAIT
missions._rules: MISSION-AQUEDUCT.md (SPEC.md §14). Balanced at M42 (DECISIONS.md): the default timer is the longest, 6 (it was 4: a first charge on a short timer left the others no time to be set to the same turn, and one bang is the alert budget); the boat in on 15 and gone with 17 stands, measured; on Hard it stays two turns. Its two rules: `canisters` (the men jump with none; three canisters of two) and `exfil.opensTurn` (the boat is in on 15, gone at dawn, 18). A sapper has room for two charges, so the sappers and Nunn carry five at full pace. Time pencils as on the airfield. The patrols set out on turn 2. The aqueduct calls one squad down the road when it goes; the road bridge down stops the reserve and the squads (the exchange's payoff in France).
missions._enemies: M41b, the operator's: with men all round it, a reserve squad that could not be killed read as a fault. Here it can be, and one more comes down the road for it (rules reserve.replacements).

easy.summary: The aqueduct takes three charges, and no squad comes down the road when it goes.

hard.summary: The aqueduct takes five charges of your six, two squads come down the road when it goes (none once the Road Bridge is down), and the boat stays two turns, not three.

missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop into the mountains of southern Italy.
missions._words: M41. Placeholder copy for the operator to reword. The line words are asked for by every mission: nothing here has a line to cut, and `lineIsDown` is what stops the squads coming, the road bridge. The diversion is the RAF again, as in 1941: bombers over Foggia.

words.lineIsDown: the Road Bridge is already down
words.cleanOrders: Getting in and out with as little enemy attention as possible earns a special bonus!

missions._dialogue: M43: only the lines that name France or its ground (Fitch's cabbages, Vance's church, Barrow's trees and bridge), and Nunn's, who carries no spare down here: nobody jumps with a charge. Placeholder copy for the operator to reword.

fitch.onLand: Down soft as you like. Whose olives are these?

vance.onLand: I can see the aqueduct from here. We're about right.

barrow.onLand: Missed every tree in Italy. Told you I would.
barrow.onWounded: Leave it. Get to the aqueduct.

nunn.onLand: Nothing to carry down, Sarge. Where's that canister?

missions._pictures: M43. Its own pictures, each a slot that falls back until the operator's painting is in the folder (ART-PROMPTS.md Priorities 19 to 21): `enemyChips`, the garrison's chips, Italian here, tried type by type before assets/enemies (the German ones); `portraits`, the six in winter kit, tried man by man before assets/portraits; `titleCard`, its own painting, France's until the file is there.
missions._ratings: M42, set against the bot's winning scores on Normal (SCORES=1): the naive bot's middle half is 26 to 31 (North 23 to 29), the tidy bot's 22 to 28 with no kills, and a stick that takes the Road Bridge too scores 32 to 35, its best quarter 35 and over. The job with every man out unseen, the Road Bridge and a clean run is 35 before kills.
